title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 7th District
area: Northwestern and central New Jersey, including all or part of Hunterdon, Morris, Somerset, Union, Warren, and Essex counties.

context.text: Incumbent Thomas Kean Jr. won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed. Rebecca Bennett won a contested Democratic primary with 45.3% of the vote against Tina Shah, Brian Varela, and Michael Roth.

Ballotpedia identifies NJ-7 as a 2026 battleground race. Kean flipped the seat in 2022 by three points, defeating then-Rep. Tom Malinowski; Donald Trump won the district by one point in 2024 and Gov. Mikie Sherrill carried it by two points in 2025. As of August 11, 2026, the district had roughly 19,000 more registered Republicans than Democrats, and forecasters rated the race a Toss-up or Lean/Tilt Democratic.

According to Ballotpedia's summary of Politico's coverage, Democrats say they are confident about the race in part because of a months-long, previously undisclosed absence from Congress by Kean, along with President Trump's endorsement of Kean and Bennett's profile as a moderate Democrat.

summary.text: Thomas Kean Jr. is the Republican incumbent for New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 after previously serving in the New Jersey Senate (2003-2022, including as minority leader) and General Assembly (2001-2003). He serves on the House Foreign Affairs and Science, Space, and Technology committees and co-leads the bipartisan SALT Caucus.

background.text: Born in Livingston, New Jersey, in 1968; son of former New Jersey Gov. Thomas H. Kean, who served 1982-1990.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Dartmouth College in 1990 and a master's degree in law and diplomacy from Tufts University in 1997.

Worked at the Environmental Protection Agency during the George H.W. Bush administration, as an advisor to then-U.S. Rep. Bob Franks, and volunteered as a firefighter and EMT, later serving as vice president of a fire department.
Served in the New Jersey General Assembly (2001-2003) and the New Jersey Senate (2003-2022), including as Republican/minority leader from 2008 to 2022.

priorities.text: Says he has made affordability a top priority in Congress, including leading the fight as a member of the bipartisan SALT Caucus to fully restore the State and Local Tax deduction.
priorities.quote: I have made affordability a top priority during my time in Congress and will always continue the fight to lower the cost of living for hard working New Jersey families.

priorities.text: Cites more than $38 million in federal funding secured for community projects in the district and $62 million returned to residents through constituent casework.
Says his approach is guided by New Jersey's interests "even when it means standing up to leaders in either party," pointing to his membership in the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus.

positions.summary: As a member of the bipartisan SALT Caucus, says he led the fight to fully restore the State and Local Tax deduction, providing tax relief for homeowners in the high-tax district rather than raising their federal tax burden.
Says he is passionate about U.S. national-security interests, including standing with allies such as Israel and Ukraine.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs (including as chairman of the Europe subcommittee), the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
Introduced the Fire Grants and Safety Act, which the Senate passed.
Introduced his One-Seat-Ride Act, aimed at improving NJ Transit/Amtrak rail service into New York, which advanced in the House.

His office says he has secured nearly $39 million in federal funding through the Community Project Funding process since taking office in 2023, and closed more than 5,400 constituent casework cases, recovering nearly $66 million.
Introduced the Safer GAMING Act, which would require online video game providers to give parents tools to disable communication between a minor and other users on gaming platforms.

Introduced the Mental Health Parity Enforcement and Funding Act, which would give the U.S. Department of Labor authority to investigate and hold insurers accountable for violating the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act of 2008, and would extend supplemental funding for enforcement.

candidates.name: Rebecca Bennett
candidates.ballotNote: Won a contested June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.3% of the vote against Tina Shah (20.0%), Brian Varela (19.1%), and Michael Roth (15.6%).

summary.text: Rebecca Bennett is the Democratic nominee for New Jersey's 7th Congressional District. A former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and test pilot who later became a healthcare executive, she was previously a registered Republican and switched parties in July 2016. She is campaigning on affordability, healthcare, and national security.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from the Texas Academy of Mathematics and Science and a bachelor's degree from Cornell University on an ROTC scholarship before commissioning into the U.S. Navy.

Served more than 15 years in the Navy and Air National Guard as a helicopter pilot, experimental test pilot, and aircraft commander, flying the MH-60 Seahawk; became the 18th female U.S. Naval Test Pilot School graduate.

Earned an MBA from the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School using the GI Bill, then built a career in healthcare, including at Johnson & Johnson and in digital health, obesity, and gastrointestinal care.
Currently serves as vice president of strategic partnerships and network operations at Oshi Health.
Was previously a registered Republican and switched her registration to Democratic in July 2016.

priorities.text: Holding the current administration accountable, saying Congress has "abdicated its responsibility to be an equal branch of government."
priorities.quote: The current Congress has completely abdicated its responsibility to be an equal branch of government.

priorities.text: Affordability, including bringing down costs for New Jersey families amid inflation and the rising cost of living.
Healthcare, drawing on her private-sector experience to expand access and bring down costs for patients.
National security, citing her military background and the growing use of AI and drones in warfare.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will work in Congress to restore a woman's right to choose at the federal level and ensure New Jersey women's reproductive rights are not infringed upon.
Says she would protect people with pre-existing conditions and restore Medicaid and Medicare funding, which she says Kean and Republicans cut.

Campaign website says she supports "commonsense, popular gun safety reforms," restrictions on weapons she describes as "weapons of war," reimplementing the tax on gun silencers, and restoring CDC gun-violence research funding.
Campaign website says she would maintain environmental regulations, invest in climate-resilient infrastructure, and incentivize renewable energy and electric vehicles.
Campaign website says she would fully restore the SALT deduction so New Jersey taxpayers are not double-taxed.

candidates.name: Seamus O'Toole

summary.text: Seamus O'Toole is running in New Jersey's 7th Congressional District on the "Stop Israel's Genocide Party" ballot line.
